description: Hydraulic component library showcase. A SpeedSource (150 rad/s) drives a 10 cm^3/rev FixedDisplacementPump (eta_v 0.95, eta_m 0.9) from a 1 bar Tank into a 20 cm^3 pump line protected by a PressureReliefValve (100 bar, 5 bar regulation range); a CheckValve (1 bar cracking) feeds a 50 cm^3 rail, a 2 m, 10 mm hose (Pipe, N = 2, f_t = 0.03) connects the rail to a 0.2 l Accumulator (50 bar precharge, n = 1.4), and a DirectionalValve43 (A_max 1e-5 m^2, 2% overlap) driven by 0.4*sin(pi*(t - 0.5)) from 0.5 s extends the HydraulicCylinder (stroke 0.5 m) with a 100 kg load and a 2000 N*s/m damper until 1.5 s, retracts it until 2.5 s and extends again. Every hydraulic law is smooth, so the only event is the spool sine's start.

checks.note: the relief valve caps the pump line at p_set + dp_reg above the 1 bar tank (measured max 101.24 bar)
the rail behind the check valve stays below the relief limit as well (measured max 101.40 bar, a hose pressure wave on charging)
charged and at rest: the relief valve regulates the pump line where it passes the whole pump flow, 1.24 bar into its 5 bar regulation range
at rest all of the pump flow (2.274e-4 m^3/s, eta_v at 100 bar) goes over the relief valve
the check valve blocks the reverse flow from the rail and the accumulator: only its leakage (measured min -2e-11 m^3/s)
end of the first extension (measured 0.09769 m)
the rod stays inside the stroke
the rod stays inside the 0.5 m stroke (measured max 0.0977 m)
the pump only dissipates (leakage plus friction; 393.5 W at 100 bar)
the accumulator supplies the stroke flow above the pump flow and keeps the rail above 70 bar (measured min 74.05 bar at 1.21 s)
no solver failure, no connection or causality error, no algebraic loop (every valve sits between compliances) and no event-limit stop
